data.hook: Rams fans watched their Super Bowl dreams crash in a 27-7 loss to the 49ers on September 10 in Melbourne, Australia. Suddenly, their team stood alone as the division's only 0-1 squad.
data.name: Rams Sit Alone in Last in NFC West After 49ers Rout
data.summary: The Los Angeles Rams lost big to the San Francisco 49ers in the NFL's first regular-season game Down Under, dropping to 0-1 while the Seahawks and Cardinals also won their openers. Preseason hype had painted the star-studded Rams as unbeatable, even with bold predictions of an undefeated run and another Super Bowl, but the lopsided defeat sparked waves of fan disappointment and dark humor online. One fan captured the shock: 'We went from Rams are unbeatable and Super Bowl locks to are the Rams in trouble in less than a week.' The team now faces the Giants at home in Week 2.

data.hook: Myles Garrett pushed through knee pain in the Rams' opener but called it his worst game ever. Now, surgery means he'll miss at least four games.
data.name: Rams Place Myles Garrett on Injured Reserve After Knee Surgery
data.summary: The Rams acquired the two-time Defensive Player of the Year in a blockbuster offseason trade from the Cleveland Browns, but a lingering knee injury forced arthroscopic surgery. Garrett sat out most of training camp, struggled in the 27-7 season-opening loss to the 49ers in Australia with zero tackles or sacks, and now heads to injured reserve. He'll miss matchups against the Giants, Broncos, Eagles, and Bills, with a possible return in Week 6 against the Cardinals on Oct. 18. The team turns to edge rushers like Byron Young while awaiting Aaron Donald's impact.

data.hook: Rookie Taylen Green, the speedy sixth-rounder from Arkansas, suits up as the Browns' emergency third quarterback against the Jaguars. He'll only see the field if both Watson and Sanders go down.
data.name: Browns Name Rookie Green Emergency Third QB for Opener
data.summary: The Cleveland Browns released their inactive list for Sunday's season opener in Jacksonville, listing Green as the third emergency QB with no special plays planned. The list also sidelines linebacker Justin Jefferson, cornerback Noah Igbinoghene, safety Daniel Thomas, cornerback Toriano Pride Jr., center Parker Brailsford, and guard Teven Jenkins due to injuries like Jenkins' back issue and Brailsford's thumb problem. The team elevated linebacker Nathaniel Watson and cornerback D’Angelo Ross from the practice squad, keeping backup Shedeur Sanders ready while saving Green's athleticism for a true crisis.
